findings.why_it_matters: The markdown heading depth resets at every PDF page break instead of tracking the clause number, so D.2.2.2 is emitted at '##' - the same level as the '## Page 1036' scaffolding heading and two levels ABOVE its own parent D.2.2 ('####'). In any generated table of contents or heading-driven navigation, D.2.2.2 through D.2.2.5.3 detach from D.2.2 and read as peers of the annex itself. No normative text is lost (the clause number is preserved inline in the heading text), so this is structural, not normative. It is systemic and NOT confined to this batch: 'grep -n "^#\+ D\.2\(\.\|$\| \)" specs/ISO_COBOL.md' shows the same reset at every page boundary in Annex D (D.2.3.2.3 at '##' under D.2.3.2 at '###', D.2.3.3.3 at '##' under D.2.3.3 at '##', D.2.4.3.1 at '##' vs sibling D.2.4.3.2 at '###', etc.), and the document-wide level census (2304 '##', 1413 '###', 96 '####') is consistent with a page-local reset rather than a clause-depth mapping.
findings.suggested_repair: Do NOT hand-edit these headings. Fix it in the transcription/normalization tool: derive the markdown heading level from the dotted clause number (depth = number of dot-separated components, offset by a fixed base) rather than from the heading's ordinal position on the current PDF page, then re-emit. Verify with a script that asserts, for every '^#+ <clause-number> ' heading, level(child) == level(parent)+1.
